notes: `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` section 10.1, Task 5: verify `T↑ ⊆ T` under the sound views `Vo = To` and `Ve = Te`. Global schema `{E}` (binary) with the standard left-linear transitive closure; local schema `{Vo, Ve}`, whose relations are source tables, with `T↑(x, y) :- Vo(x, y)` and `T↑(x, y) :- Ve(x, y)`; the views themselves are the odd/even path program over `E`.

The source documents the reformulations task document (sha256 `32a3ac6b428d851f0aaa4fb7acdbf2fe4ad5dacca93ee118837888ff91b7a1c6`) and `reports/VerificationTasks.pdf` (sha256 `796ff97c082c6fc70e75a60c0dd40ec0680b738d7184a8b8aefea8c681b3ebff`) carry the same section 10.1 text, so both name this task.

The command is not hand-authored: `Fidelity/Example4034.lean` states the PDF's three Datalog programs, compiles each with `Datalog.WhielCompiler.Naive`, writes the three compiled commands one after the other (the reformulation, the views, then the global closure), renames the generated snapshots `TUp_1`, `To_1`, `Te_1` and `T_1` to the auxiliary input names `TUp_aux`, `To_aux`, `Te_aux` and `T_aux`, and proves the result equal to `inputCmd` by `decide +kernel`; the same module fixes `inputPre` as `true` and `inputPost` as the claim and pins the single loop `Hoare.preprocess` computes from the sequence.

The soundness hypothesis refers to the least fixpoints `To` and `Te` that the loop computes, so it cannot be a first-order precondition; the precondition is `true` and the postcondition states `(¬((Vo ⊆ To) ∧ (Ve ⊆ Te))) ∨ (TUp ⊆ T)`, the reference's formulation of `(Vo ⊆ To ∧ Ve ⊆ Te) → TUp ⊆ T`. `Vo` and `Ve` are never assigned, so at exit the hypothesis compares the given sources with the computed views.
Expected verdict valid: `Vo ∪ Ve ⊆ To ∪ Te = T`. Nothing is certified in this pass, so the classification stays `unknown`.

Reference encoding for intent only: `origin/reformulation-multiview:Benchmark/Example4034/Input.lean` at commit `7b793fe36c02d051a0771d110333d1c9bbca40cd`, an `IndexAlphaName` hand-written input in the earlier single-level framework. Nothing is copied from it.

Interpretation: the PDF's task line writes `Vo = To` and `ve = Te` while calling the views sound (non-exact LAV); sound views are `Vo ⊆ To`, `Ve ⊆ Te`, the reading of the reference encoding and of this one. The encoded statement (containment hypothesis) is stronger than the equality reading, so the expected verdict is unaffected.
title: Containment of a reformulation over sound odd/even views in transitive closure
explanation: The global program T is the standard right-linear transitive closure of E. The local reformulation is loop-free: TUp is simply the union of two source relations Vo and Ve, which stand for odd- and even-length path views computed by a separate odd/even mutual-recursion program over E, but are only assumed sound (Vo ⊆ To, Ve ⊆ Te) rather than exact. Because that soundness hypothesis refers to the least fixpoints the loop itself computes, it cannot be phrased as a precondition, so it is folded into the postcondition as an implication written with ¬ and ∨: if Vo and Ve are sound approximations of the odd/even path relations, then the reformulation is contained in transitive closure, TUp ⊆ T. This is a conditional (soundness-guarded) containment claim. The claim is valid, since Vo ∪ Ve ⊆ To ∪ Te = T whenever the hypothesis holds.
preInWords: The precondition is simply true; no constraint holds at entry.
postInWords: The postcondition states that if Vo is contained in the odd-length-path relation To and Ve is contained in the even-length-path relation Te, then the reformulation TUp is contained in the transitive closure T.
